account:
Something unusually large is being arranged at the town hall: a community gathering at eighteen today, with lanterns and two hundred feast loaves. Yesterday I saw builder and innkeeper putting bread in a hall table chest. Neighbour said innkeeper paid the baker for a large catering order, and today baker said innkeeper had verified that all two hundred loaves arrived. Builder appears involved with supplies and lighting, innkeeper with catering, and other local helpers with organising. Secretary knows about the gathering and has arranged an escort to meet me at the office shortly beforehand. Innkeeper has invited me and says I need no prepared remarks.

I suspect this is a planned community feast, possibly a surprise celebration, but I do not know its occasion or whom it celebrates. My direct questions have not yet produced that explanation. I should not mistake that uncertainty for proof of anything sinister.

There is also a repeated rumour about a bridge or port change at the bakery. I have heard townsfolk repeat it, but nobody has supplied a concrete change. Baker explicitly says it is unverified, and I have told baker and neighbour that I know of no confirmed bridge or ferry change. It may simply be circulating gossip rather than connected to the feast.

I went to the mill for my ten o'clock grain inspection but did not obtain a proper stock report. Baker bought eight hay bales at the mill stall this morning and says the miller is responsible for the full stocks; that does not establish whether there is a shortage. I am now home for noon lunch. My remaining appointments are council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the gathering at eighteen with an escort.
